summary: Quarterly health review focused on recent spike in inference spend, regional latency variance, and upcoming rollout of patient-facing summarization. Agreed pilot scope for Dedicated pool evaluation and immediate cost mitigations (prefix caching, token limits).
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-04-07 15:30 UTC · Duration 52m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Tom (Redwood SE), Liam (CSM), Sofia (HelioMed), Markus (HelioMed), Priya (HelioMed), Daniel (HelioMed)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for hopping on, um we'll try to keep this tight, 45 minutes ish and then leave time for action items.
[00:12] Sofia: Yeah appreciate it, we got some finance people on because the invoice this month was, uh, a bit of a surprise.
[00:18] Daniel: Hey all, Daniel from finance. The spike looks like March 21-24, want to understand what drove it.
[00:25] Tom: quick note — we ran the traces you sent, there's a pattern where the KV cache hit rate drops during long-running sessions and then you get prefix replay. Could explain token overages.
[00:38] Markus: when you say KV cache, are you meaning the prefix cache on the Dedicated instances? We thought cache was enabled across the board.
[00:45] Tom: yes, the K V cache — but it's sensitive to session affinity; if requests jump regions or pods are cycled you lose the cache warming. Also tuning the cache TTL helps.
[00:57] Priya: I want to be clear on two things — latency to EU users and cost per call. Our mobile summarization flow has tight SLOs, users drop at 800ms median.
[01:10] Maya: understood. High level — three buckets of mitigation: routing (region pinning), runtime (KV/cache + quantization), and usage (prompt pruning & token limits). We'll scope a small dedicated pool pilot to test runtime changes.
[01:25] Sofia: what's the difference in unit cost if we move to a small Dedicated pool versus hosted on demand?
[01:31] Maya: rough numbers: Hosted opex per token is variable; Dedicated amortizes GPU hours. For your current volume, Dedicated with light autoscale looks ~20-35% cheaper assuming steady traffic. But depends on burst patterns and utilization.
[01:46] Daniel: that 20-35% delta — does that factor in egress and S3 storage for prompt history?
[01:51] Maya: good point — our rough calc excludes third-party egress; we'll send a billing breakdown with egress assumptions.
[01:58] Markus: we've got multi-region users and the spike was correlated with a release that increased session length, so maybe more tokens per session.
[02:08] Tom: yep that matches logs — average tokens per session went from ~340 to ~1,120 after the March release. That multiplied cost even with stable request counts.
[02:18] Priya: so immediate quick wins?
[02:20] Tom: short-term: add prefix trimming, enforce a 512 token cap on summarization pipeline, enable sticky routing for long sessions, and increase KV cache TTL. Medium-term: run Dedicated pilot with quantization profile (int8 q4) and measure p99 latency.
[02:36] Sofia: For the pilot, what telemetry will we get? We need token-level cost, per-region p50/p95/p99, and per-route error breakdown.
[02:45] Liam: the Redwood Console will provide token-level cost, route dashboards, and traces; we'll share a sample dashboard.
[02:52] Daniel: tell me more about degradation — if Dedicated goes down what's fallback?
[02:56] Maya: automatic fallback to hosted variants, policy-based routing (we can set a canary with 10% to Dedicated then shift). There is a cost delta during fallback.
[03:05] Markus: we had questions about security — SOC2, SSO, and KMS. We need those docs, and also audit logs retention for 1 year.
[03:13] Maya: yes, we'll share SOC2 report and SSO integration notes; Private deployment options with customer-managed KMS exist if needed. Audit logs 1 year is supported via enterprise retention add-on.
[03:24] Sofia: ok good. Another thing — we're seeing a lot of small repeated calls from a background job, looks like retries inflating token counts.
[03:33] Priya: that was added to improve reliability but maybe backfired. Can we get a recommendation on debounce and caching?
[03:38] Tom: recommend batching at the job level, TTL-based caching for identical prompts, and a jittered retry backoff. We'll provide a runbook.
[03:47] [04:00] Maya: walking through the billing spike — Tom you mentioned token increase per session — can you share visual?
[04:04] Tom: yes, we prepared a quick heatmap — sending link in chat (link: /redwood/billing/heliomed/march-spike). Observations: token-per-session jump, and region mismatch causing cache churn.
[04:18] Sofia: For prioritization, we need low-effort wins. What's easiest?
[04:21] Maya: immediate items: 1) enforce token cap; 2) enable sticky routing for sessions longer than X minutes; 3) apply prefix trimming to stored contexts. Those are low-risk and reversible.
[04:33] Daniel: cost modelling — can you run scenarios for commit levels 100k, 250k, 500k tokens per day and show break-even for Dedicated?
[04:42] Maya: yes we'll run three scenarios and show amortized GPU cost.
[04:46] Priya: on rollout plan — we want to pilot Dedicated in EU first for 2 weeks with 10% traffic, then expand. Any gotchas?
[04:55] Tom: watch for cold starts and cache warm-up. Also quantization can change some model behaviors; we'll do regression checks on your prompt set.
[05:05] Sofia: regression checks — how thorough? We need to ensure hallucination rate doesn't increase.
[05:09] Tom: we'll run similarity and rouge-like checks on outputs; and sample human review on flagged prompts. Also Redwood Optimize will flag regressions tied to prompt sets.
[05:19] Markus: about rollback — if we see quality dip, what's the tactical step?
[05:22] Maya: immediate rollback to hosted model variant, pause canary, and investigate quantization artifacts. We keep model version pins for quick rollback.
[05:30] [06:00] Daniel: what's the SLA if we do Dedicated? We looked for 99.9% but want to know realistic p99 latency commitments.
[06:08] Maya: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and target latency tiers; we'll surface expected p99 latency for your config in the pilot plan.
[06:14] Priya: can the console alert us on cost anomalies? We want proactive alerts if daily spend exceeds expected by 15%.
[06:20] Liam: yes we can set alert rules on token burn rate and model route spend; we can push to Slack and email.
[06:27] Sofia: ok let's recap pilot timeline and owners.
[06:30] Maya: recap — action items: Maya send billing breakdown and pilot pricing; Tom run KV-cache/latency benchmark and prepare regression suite; Priya provide 50-sample prioritized prompt set; Daniel confirm commit range; Liam to share dashboard template and set initial alerts.
[06:49] Markus: can you also include a note on estimated warm-up time for Dedicated pool? We need to plan capacity windows.
[06:55] Tom: estimate: 30-90 minutes for cache warp and warm-up depending on traffic pattern; we'll include warm-up plan.
[07:03] Sofia: last Q — if we enable prefix trimming, do we risk losing important context?
[07:07] Tom: tradeoff, yes. We'll test heuristics: preserve last N tokens for user state and trim earlier tokens. We'll include best-practice heuristics in runbook.
[07:20] Maya: great, we'll follow up with doc links and the pilot workbook. Any other items?
[07:25] Priya: nothing else from me.
[07:27] Daniel: all good.
[07:30] Maya: thanks team, we'll land the materials by next week and sync mid-pilot.
[07:35] [END]

Post-call notes: shared links referenced in chat: /redwood/docs/dedicated-pilot-workbook, /redwood/billing/heliomed/march-spike, /redwood/security/soc2-2026.pdf
Decisions made: scope Dedicated pilot in EU with 10% traffic for 2 weeks; implement immediate low-effort mitigations (token cap, sticky routing, prefix trimming); finance to validate commit range.
